critical_code_review_comments: CAMERA BUG ROOT CAUSE IDENTIFIED AND FIXED:
- Problem: When track.enabled changes, MediaStream reference stays the same
- React doesn't detect the change because object reference is unchanged
- Solution: streamKey counter forces re-evaluation of memoized displayStream
FIX VERIFICATION - All critical paths covered:
1. Toggle video ON/OFF mid-call: streamKey bumped in toggleVideo (lines 691, 743)
2. Join with camera off: track.enabled synced in joinMeeting (lines 588-595)
3. Display update: displayStream memo includes streamKey dependency (line 389)
4. Tile re-render: ParticipantTile useEffect includes video_enabled (line 91)
5. Grid re-render: VideoGrid uses streamKey in key prop (line 1091)
- User toggles video OFF before joining → track.enabled synced at join time
- User toggles camera ON/OFF multiple times → streamKey increments each time
- Virtual background enabled/disabled → displayStream properly switches
- Comprehensive console.log debugging statements for troubleshooting
- Proper error handling with user-friendly messages
- CSS opacity approach avoids DOM thrashing (video element always rendered)
- Track state verification: hasVideoTrack checks enabled && readyState === 'live'

camera_bug_fix_analysis.root_cause: When track.enabled changes on a MediaStream, the stream reference doesn't change, so React's shallow comparison doesn't detect the update
camera_bug_fix_analysis.solution: streamKey counter that increments on any video toggle, included in displayStream memo deps and VideoGrid key prop
affected_scenarios: User joins without camera enabled, then turns it on mid-call
User toggles camera on/off multiple times during call
User turns off camera in preview, then joins meeting
fix_locations: Lines 382-389: displayStream memo with streamKey dependency

notes: Camera bug fix has been properly implemented. The core issue was that MediaStream track.enabled changes don't change the stream reference, so React couldn't detect the change. The streamKey mechanism forces re-evaluation. All critical code paths have been verified through code review. Actual camera testing requires real hardware which is not available in headless browser environment.
